The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\sqrt{2}+1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}\,\text{d}x=(\sqrt{2}+1)\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}\,\text{d}x=(\sqrt{2}+1)\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
